title: Gebisa Ejeta
style_block: Rich oil painting style with textured canvas grain, warm amber and earth-toned palette, volumetric golden hour light, and organic tactile detail.
world_block: Any person is Black and Ethiopian, with deep brown skin and short black natural hair; any hands or feet are deep brown. Any villager in rural Ethiopia wears a traditional white hand-woven cotton shawl (gabi or netela) over plain cotton clothes, never a modern T-shirt, jeans or a suit. Any village home is a round mud-walled hut with a conical thatched roof (tukul). Any sorghum has tall stalks with heavy, rounded, reddish-brown seed heads; it is not wheat and not maize. The time is the 1950s to the 1990s.

reference_sheet.prompt: A reference sheet with no people in it: the Ethiopian highland landscape with terraced fields and deep amber soil, a field of sorghum, one round thatched tukul in the distance, and a few pieces of laboratory glassware holding green sprouts, in warm golden-hour light with a rich painterly canvas texture.

music.caption: An inspiring contemporary instrumental score featuring gentle warm strings, subtle East African pentatonic lyre accents, and delicate ambient pads. Designed as a soft background texture under narration, it evolves smoothly with no aggressive lead melody.

narration.en: Why would a young boy walk twenty kilometres across Ethiopia every Sunday evening just to attend primary school?

shots.subtitle_en: Why would a young boy walk twenty kilometres across Ethiopia every Sunday evening just to attend primary school?

narration.en: Gebisa Ejeta was born in Wollonkomi to Oromo parents, encouraged constantly by his mother to pursue education.

shots.subtitle_en: Gebisa Ejeta was born in Wollonkomi to Oromo parents, encouraged constantly by his mother to pursue education.
shots.reason: Evokes deep cultural respect for mothers and the transformative power of quiet family encouragement.

shots.image_prompt: A young man seen from behind, standing at a vista looking out over rich agricultural terraced fields under soft morning light.
shots.motion_prompt: the grain sways in the wind, the young man stands still looking out over the fields, slow tilt up

narration.en: He intended to study engineering, but his mother convinced him he could accomplish more working in agriculture.

shots.subtitle_en: He intended to study engineering, but his mother convinced him he could accomplish more working in agriculture.
shots.reason: Highlights the critical pivotal choice to dedicate one's life to feeding the land.

narration.en: After studying at Haramaya University, Ejeta earned his doctorate in plant breeding from Purdue University in 1978.

shots.subtitle_en: After studying at Haramaya University, Ejeta earned his doctorate in plant breeding from Purdue University in 1978.
shots.reason: Shows academic dedication and the transition from traditional farming to world-class scientific inquiry.

shots.motion_prompt: heat shimmers over the cracked ground, the single green shoot trembles in the wind, slow pull back

narration.en: He went to work in rain-starved northern Sudan, researching sorghum crops for five straight years.

shots.subtitle_en: He went to work in rain-starved northern Sudan, researching sorghum crops for five straight years.
shots.reason: Dramatizes the extreme hardship of hunger and drought that science was called upon to solve.

narration.en: His drought-tolerant hybrid produced yields up to 150 percent higher, covering one million acres in Sudan yearly.

shots.subtitle_en: His drought-tolerant hybrid produced yields up to 150 percent higher, covering one million acres in Sudan yearly.

narration.en: At Purdue, he developed a mechanism to stop parasitic Striga weeds from attacking sorghum crops.

shots.subtitle_en: At Purdue, he developed a mechanism to stop parasitic Striga weeds from attacking sorghum crops.
